neighborhoods.summary: The original 1610 town-planning core, anchored by the Santa Fe Plaza and the Palace of the Governors; the densest concentration of historic adobe/Pueblo Revival architecture, galleries, and restaurants.
The city's highest concentration of art galleries, showcasing Southwestern, Indigenous, and contemporary art; a major draw for collectors and tourists.
Home to several of the city's art and folk-art museums and the site of the annual Santa Fe International Folk Art Market.
A redeveloped rail-corridor district including SITE Santa Fe contemporary art space and a farmers market.
An established residential neighborhood on the site of the former WWII internment camp; today an ordinary Santa Fe residential area.

places.description: Museum devoted to the work of Georgia O'Keeffe and artists she influenced.
State museum of modern and contemporary Southwestern art, near the Plaza.

places.place_name: New Mexico History Museum / Palace of the Governors
places.description: State history museum located behind the historic Palace of the Governors on the Plaza.

places.place_name: Meow Wolf: House of Eternal Return
places.description: Large-scale immersive art installation and collective, opened 2016.
Outdoor opera venue staging productions from late June to late August each year.

places.place_name: Cathedral Basilica of St. Francis of Assisi
places.description: The city's historic Catholic cathedral basilica on the Plaza.
Considered among the oldest church buildings in the United States (built 1610).
State capitol building, built in Territorial Revival style.
The city's ski resort, about 16 miles (26 km) northeast of downtown in the Sangre de Cristo Mountains.
24.4-mile multi-use trail network starting within about 2 miles of the Plaza.
Historic Ancestral Pueblo site approximately 30 miles from Santa Fe; a common day trip.
Public community college serving Santa Fe.
Santa Fe's own airport; American Airlines to Dallas/Fort Worth and Phoenix, United to Denver (seasonal), JSX to Dallas Love Field.

transport_airports.name: Santa Fe Regional Airport (KSAF)
transport_airports.summary: City's own airport; American Airlines (Dallas/Fort Worth, Phoenix), United (Denver, seasonal), JSX (Dallas Love Field).

transport_airports.name: Albuquerque International Sunport (ABQ)
transport_airports.summary: Larger regional airport roughly 65 miles from Santa Fe with more nonstop domestic service; Groome Transportation's Santa Fe shuttle service has ended (per Wikipedia citation), so ground transport options should be reverified before relying on a scheduled shuttle.

transport_airports.name: New Mexico Rail Runner Express
transport_airports.summary: Commuter rail connecting Santa Fe (4 stations) to Albuquerque metro area.

taxes_finance.summary: New Mexico imposes a state personal income tax in addition to federal tax (unlike Florida in the existing Batch 1 benchmark, which has none). Specific current bracket rates were not independently fetched this pass - left UNKNOWN rather than fabricated.

healthcare_insurance.system_summary: Standard U.S. healthcare system; Santa Fe is served by CHRISTUS St. Vincent Regional Medical Center as the principal hospital (name recalled from general knowledge of the city, not independently verified via a dedicated fetch this pass - flagged for re-verification).
healthcare_insurance.medicare_applicability: Fully applicable for eligible U.S. beneficiaries.
healthcare_insurance.unknown_reason: Hospital-specific and network-specific details not independently fetched this pass.

lifestyle_derivation_notes: Santa Fe: high desert / mountain foothill setting (Sangre de Cristo Mountains), no beach/coastal access, strong arts/culture/dining scene, nearby skiing (Ski Santa Fe ~26km), hiking/trail access strong (Dale Ball Trails network from downtown), golf present in the region but not confirmed at a specific named course this pass, historic/UNESCO Creative City character, moderate-to-strong retirement/tourism orientation given large arts-tourism economy and high proportion of over-65 residents (24.3% per 2020 census).

housing_property.restrictions_summary: Domestic US relocation; no foreign-buyer restriction applies to US citizens.
housing_property.property_tax_notes: New Mexico property tax is assessed at the county level (Santa Fe County); rates and exemptions require parcel-specific confirmation.

lgbtq_inclusivity.legal_protections: Nationwide US marriage equality since Obergefell v. Hodges (2015); New Mexico has state-level nondiscrimination protections covering sexual orientation and gender identity.
lgbtq_inclusivity.social_acceptance: HIGH - Santa Fe has a long-established, visible LGBTQ+ community.
lgbtq_inclusivity.community_scene: Established local scene with Santa Fe Pride events.
lgbtq_inclusivity.evidence_summary: Federal and state legal protections plus a historically welcoming arts-community culture.

safety_risks.summary: Numbeo crime index 48.76 (Moderate); safety index 51.24 (Moderate) - broadly average for a small US city, with property-crime concerns noted by contributors.
safety_risks.mitigation_notes: Standard urban precautions; verify neighborhood-level conditions before choosing housing.

safety_risks.summary: Northern New Mexico has real wildfire risk in dry years, particularly in surrounding forested/mountain areas.
safety_risks.mitigation_notes: Check property-specific wildfire-zone designation and defensible-space requirements.

connectivity_remote_work.coworking_summary: Coworking options exist given Santa Fe's remote-work-friendly, arts/tech-adjacent population, but require listing-level confirmation.
connectivity_remote_work.us_time_zone_fit: America/Denver - Mountain Time, good overlap with all continental US time zones.
connectivity_remote_work.remote_work_notes: US national broadband figures are strong, but actual Santa Fe/rural New Mexico speeds vary by provider and address; verify at the specific property.

language_integration.integration_notes: English is the primary language; Spanish is also widely spoken given Santa Fe's Hispanic/Nuevomexicano heritage, useful but not required.

pets.import_requirements: NOT_APPLICABLE - domestic US relocation; standard interstate health-certificate requirements apply, not international import rules.
pets.dog_parks_summary: Multiple parks and open-space trails support dog-friendly living (e.g., Frenchy's Field Park).

community_social.summary: Long-established arts/culture retirement destination with a strong creative and outdoors-oriented community; New Mexico's largest concentration of galleries outside major metros.
community_social.clubs_groups: Extensive arts organizations, opera/music societies, and outdoor-recreation clubs.
community_social.transient_vs_rooted: More rooted, with seasonal tourism influx
community_social.source_name: General knowledge of Santa Fe's arts economy

accessibility.sidewalk_quality: Historic Plaza-area surfaces variable; newer areas generally standard
accessibility.hills_terrain: Moderate - high-desert terrain, some grade changes
accessibility.accessible_transit: LIMITED - car-dependent city with modest public transit
accessibility.mobility_notes: Mobility fit requires neighborhood and building-level review; Santa Fe's historic core has narrow, uneven adobe-era sidewalks.
accessibility.source_name: General knowledge of Santa Fe urban geography

bureaucracy_setup.typical_documents: Proof of address; driver's license transfer; utility setup

work_business.major_industries: State government, arts/tourism, opera/performing arts, and a growing tech/science sector (proximity to Los Alamos National Laboratory).
work_business.employment_notes: US citizens have full nationwide work authorization; local job market is tourism/arts/government-weighted.
work_business.work_authorization: NOT_APPLICABLE - domestic US relocation, full work rights.
work_business.remote_work_suitability: STRONG - Mountain Time zone overlaps well with all continental US business hours.
work_business.source_name: General knowledge of Santa Fe's economy

retirement_aging.medicare_notes: Medicare is fully applicable for eligible US beneficiaries nationwide, including Santa Fe.
retirement_aging.social_security_notes: US Social Security applies without cross-border complications for domestic relocation.
retirement_aging.retirement_notes: Retirement fit is strong for arts/culture-oriented retirees but should account for high-altitude (7,000 ft) adjustment and dry-climate health considerations.
retirement_aging.source_name: General US Medicare/Social Security domestic-relocation facts

lifestyle_laws.important_rules: No visa or work-permit considerations apply.

reality_check.title: High-altitude and dry-climate adjustment is real
reality_check.detail: Santa Fe sits at roughly 7,000 feet elevation with a semi-arid high-desert climate; some newcomers experience altitude and dry-climate adjustment effects.

reality_check.title: Housing costs are high for a small city
reality_check.detail: City-centre 1-bedroom rents average over $2,200/month, reflecting strong tourism-driven demand relative to Santa Fe's small population.

move_checklist.task: Budget for above-average rent given tourism-driven demand
move_checklist.description: City-centre 1BR rents commonly exceed $2,200/month; verify current listings before committing.

move_checklist.task: Plan for high-altitude and dry-climate adjustment
move_checklist.description: Discuss altitude/hydration considerations with a physician, especially for those with cardiovascular or respiratory conditions.

move_checklist.task: Review wildfire risk for specific properties
move_checklist.description: Northern New Mexico has real seasonal wildfire risk; check defensible-space and insurance requirements.

move_checklist.task: Confirm New Mexico state tax treatment of retirement income
move_checklist.description: Verify current state tax rules for pensions/Social Security with the NM Taxation and Revenue Department.

environment_quality.air_quality_summary: Generally good; high-desert air with low humidity.
environment_quality.water_reliability: GENERALLY RELIABLE - regional water-supply planning is an ongoing concern in the arid Southwest
environment_quality.heat_humidity_comfort: Dry, comfortable summers with cool nights; cold winters at altitude
environment_quality.mosquito_pest_pressure: LOW - dry climate suppresses most pest pressure
environment_quality.wildfire_smoke_exposure: SEASONAL - regional wildfire smoke can affect air quality in dry years
environment_quality.drought_water_stress: MODERATE-HIGH - Southwest US regional water stress
environment_quality.environmental_notes: High-desert climate (~7,000 ft elevation) with strong UV exposure and low humidity year-round.

daily_life_practicality.driving_difficulty: Standard US small-city driving; limited public transit
daily_life_practicality.card_payment_acceptance: Very high - standard US card/mobile-payment acceptance
daily_life_practicality.emergency_services_summary: 911 emergency number; regional hospital network (Christus St. Vincent).
daily_life_practicality.things_residents_wish_they_knew: The high-desert climate and altitude take real physical adjustment; hydration and sun protection matter more than newcomers expect.
